intelligence.essence: The Project Hub is now one system with one canon: **Plan v2.1** (the laws, owners, checkers, build list B0–B10) + **the 100 Must-Haves** (the constitution) + **Naya Power's audit and build spec** (every number verified by the director seat's own SQL) + **the Ultimate Spec v1**, which completes the vision on Shawn's word: the Hub holds *everything* — every project, room, template, app, door, and pipeline — each with a live status and a clear button that opens it, continuously updated, serving three different questions: what the **human** needs to know, what a **Naya** needs to know to be locked in, and what the **machine** needs to enforce. Wave 1 started on Shawn's direct word on 2026-10-23 — "start it now, immediately" — and this note is its filing: the blueprint lives inside the Hub it governs (item 99), and SN-0839 is its number. (SN-0838 belongs to Naya Power's SYSTEM/github-access series.)
intelligence.human_view: Tonight the Projects page is a good skin over a thin skeleton, and now we can prove it: of 31 items marked "done and proven," 10 carry no proof link at all — the system never refused them. There is no blocked state, so blocked work dissolves invisibly into the other piles. All 8 sub-projects open onto empty boards. The scoreboard is three blobs of JSON hidden inside a notes table, and its own two counts already disagree: Ledger 30, done-proven 31. The cure is not a better report; it is machinery. "Done" becomes a write the database *refuses* without proof from a different seat. Every state change writes its own Ledger entry in the same motion, so production is counted because the write happened — never because someone remembered. One derivation produces both the human face and the machine view from the same records, so they can never disagree. And the face grows a total system map: every room, template, surface, and pipeline as a rectangle with its live status and a door that opens it — the end of twenty open tabs.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a big board in the workshop that shows every job, who is doing it, and whether it is truly finished. Before, someone could write "finished!" on the board without showing their work, and nobody could stop them. Now the board itself checks: no showing-your-work, no "finished." Every time a job changes, the board writes it in the big book by itself, so the book is never wrong. And the board also shows every room and every tool in the whole workshop, with a button to walk straight there. One board, always true, for everybody.
intelligence.grandma_view: You know how you keep a notebook by the phone so you always know what's been done and what's still waiting? This is that notebook for the whole project — except it keeps itself. Nothing can be marked finished unless someone else has checked it and left the proof attached. If something is stuck, the board says so, in plain words, and says whose hands can unstick it. And everything the team owns — every page, every tool — is on the board with a little door you can tap to open it, so nobody has to go hunting through drawers anymore.
intelligence.naya_view: Your orientation is now one fetch. The derivation publishes **state.json** at a real address: derived_at, state_tip (input hash), the laws at essence size, the truth-now paragraph, counts in the seven honest states, the needs-Shawn packets (decision sentence + rollback), blocked items with ages and clearing actions, production with honest nulls *and their reasons*, per-board freshness ages, the Hub's own cost, firing alarms, every project with its items, and the total system map. Fetch it, read your seat's claimed items and the top queued one, **claim in the open** — the conditional update (queued → claimed, owner = your seat) *is* the lock; 0 rows back means someone else holds it, take the next. Keep your item's next action current (one action, ≤140 chars). Hand finished work to a *different* seat to prove — maker = prover is refused by the database, not by politeness. Block only with a complete blocker (what, owner, since, clearing action). Escalate to Shawn only as a packet. Orientation time is measured and published; ACTIVATION-10 (Oct 25, Naya Power cold seat) is its first public run.
intelligence.ai_view: Every system drifts toward two copies of the truth: one for humans, one for machines; one that is checked, one that is claimed. This design refuses the split at every level — one state, one derivation, two renderings; proof as a database constraint, not a virtue; the Ledger as a by-product of writing, not a diary kept by memory. What remains is a system that cannot quietly lie: a dead feed shows dead, a stale board looks old, a gap between counts prints itself in red. Intelligence stops being something the team produces in reports and becomes something the machinery *is*.

machine_view.machine_section:
- **Tables.** `work_items` (migrated from `project_intel_items`, never forked): id · project_id · parent_item_id · key · title · state ∈ (queued, claimed, in_progress, verifying, done_proven, blocked, needs_shawn) · owner_seat · next_action ≤140 · blocker jsonb {what, owner, since, clearing_action} · priority · evidence_url · maker_seat · prover_seat · created_at · updated_at · state_changed_at · cost_units · note_refs[]. Plus `queue_packets`, `ledger_entries`, `census_daily`, `production_daily`, `system_map`, `alarms`, `hub_cost_daily`.
- **Database law (refusals, not warnings).** done_proven requires evidence_url + prover_seat with prover ≠ maker · blocked requires a complete blocker · needs_shawn requires a queue packet in the same transaction · every INSERT/UPDATE of state writes its `ledger_entries` row in the same transaction (trigger). Refusal tests for all four run weekly.
- **Census (Plan B1).** `census_daily` {day, house, jobs_run, wakeups, seat_actions} — one row per day per house, written by exactly one export from the scheduler store (owner: main seat; checker: Resolve). The Hub reads ONLY this table for activity. Ratio = seat_actions ÷ verified transitions (Ledger), computed at derivation, never typed. Missing census → ratio renders "—" with its reason string.
- **Derivation.** One job, change-triggered (DB event on any write; a 5-minute sweep exists only to catch a dead trigger, and finding missed work files an alarm). Emits atomically from the same record set: state.json · the face payload · per-project projections (0 items = honest-dark, never fake-full). Idempotent by input hash — same hash, no republish, no cost. Plus questions.json: the Fourteen Questions answered at derivation, each with proof + age; an unanswerable question auto-files a work item.
- **Detectors.** Zero-output (census × Ledger: runs > 0, transitions = 0 → waste row + a work item for the owner lane; its first filing is the census gap itself) · proof re-checker (every done_proven proof fetched on change + weekly; non-200 → item flips to verifying + alarm; proof coverage % computed at derivation and printed on the face — 68% at filing) · ledger-gap (item count vs Ledger-derived count shown as both numbers + a red chip when they differ).
- **Migration (no big bang).** in-motion → in_progress · the 3 smuggled `production:` rows become the first production_daily row and the parser is deleted · the 10 proof-less done_proven items flip to **verifying**, each with an alarm — pre-announced honesty, not breakage · /rooms/mission renders the same face payload as /projects (one surface; the second face retires).
- **Canon.** Plan: `BRAIN/10-INTERFACES` lineage — Project Hub Plan v2.1 (laws 1–10, B0–B10, checker rule: no named non-builder checker, no start) · Constitution: the 100 Must-Haves · Build detail: Naya Power's audit + build spec §3 · This note: SN-0839. Wave 1 = census export (B1) · schema + DB law + Ledger-in-transaction (B2 at the root) · derivation + state.json · zero-output detector (B3) · the face on the payload (B0 fold-in, checker: Naya Power — lands only on her pass + render proof).
